sections.title: 12.1 Exploring Connected Devices Using CDP and LLDP

content.text: Book pages 338 to 347. Discovery protocols let a device announce itself to its directly connected neighbors. You use them to build a map, check cabling and troubleshoot. BOOK
|  | CDP | LLDP |
| Full name | Cisco Discovery Protocol | Link Layer Discovery Protocol (IEEE 802.1AB) |
| Owner | Cisco only (proprietary) | Open standard, works across vendors |
| Default on Cisco IOS | Enabled | Disabled (needs lldp run) |
| Default timer / holdtime | 60 s / 180 s | 30 s / 120 s |
| Enable globally | cdp run (on already) | lldp run |
| Per interface | cdp enable / no cdp enable | lldp transmit and lldp receive |
| Neighbor list | show cdp neighbors | show lldp neighbors |
| Full detail | show cdp neighbors detail | show lldp neighbors detail |

Sources for the table: CDP values and the neighbor output are in the book BOOK ; the LLDP default-off state and 30/120 timers are not stated in the book and were added from Cisco documentation and secondary sources ADDED .
EXAM CRITICAL
CDP and LLDP only show directly connected devices. A switch does not pass CDP frames on, so a router connected to a switch sees the switch, not the devices behind it. BOOK
12.1.1 Getting CDP Timers and Holdtime Information

Two global CDP values matter. The timer is how often CDP packets go out every active interface. The holdtime is how long a receiver keeps a neighbor's information before discarding it if no new packet arrives. BOOK
Book output BOOK
SW-3# show cdp
Global CDP information:
Sending CDP packets every 60 seconds
Sending a holdtime value of 180 seconds
Sending CDPv2 advertisements is enabled
- show cdp: shows the global timer, holdtime and CDP version.
- Default timer 60 s and holdtime 180 s: the holdtime is three times the timer, so a neighbor survives two lost packets.
- cdp timer <5-254>: change how often packets are sent (seconds).
- cdp holdtime <10-255>: change how long neighbors keep the information (seconds).
- no cdp run / cdp run: turn CDP off or on for the whole device.
- no cdp enable / cdp enable: turn CDP off or on for one interface (interface mode).
COMMON MISTAKE
Mixing up the two. The timer controls sending. The holdtime controls how long the receiver remembers. A short holdtime with a long timer makes neighbors flap in and out of the table.
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
The book says to configure CDP "on a router" but shows the prompt of a switch (SW-3). The commands are the same on routers and switches. Minor wording issue only. UPDATED
ADDED (NOT IN THE BOOK)

Security and phones. CDP tells anyone on the link your hostname, model, IOS version and IP address. Many designs disable it on ports facing users or the Internet. Do not switch CDP off globally if you use Cisco IP phones, because the phone negotiation can depend on it. ADDED CHECK
Quick check 12.1.1
Q1. What are the default CDP timer and holdtime?
Answer: 60 s and 180 s - the receiver keeps a neighbor for 180 s.
Q2. Which command stops CDP on one interface only?
A. no cdp run
B. no cdp enable
C. cdp holdtime 0
D. no cdp timer
Answer: B - no cdp enable is per interface; no cdp run is global.
Q3. A neighbor disappears from the CDP table after a while although the cable is fine. Which value expired?
Answer: The holdtime - no CDP packet arrived within the holdtime.
12.1.2 Gathering Neighbor Information
show cdp neighbors (short form sh cdp nei) lists each directly connected device. Learn to read every column, because exam questions give you this output and ask what it means. BOOK
Based on the book's output (the book's PDF text is badly wrapped, so columns are re-aligned here) BOOK
SW-3# show cdp neighbors
Device ID Local Intrfce Holdtme Capability Platform Port ID
SW-1 Fas 0/1 150 S I WS-C3560- Fas 0/15
SW-1 Fas 0/2 150 S I WS-C3560- Fas 0/16
SW-2 Fas 0/5 162 S I WS-C3560- Fas 0/5
SW-2 Fas 0/6 162 S I WS-C3560- Fas 0/6
| Column | Meaning |
| Device ID | Hostname of the neighbor. |
| Local Intrfce | Your port that the neighbor is connected to. |
| Holdtme | Seconds left before the entry is dropped if no new CDP packet arrives (it counts down). |
| Capability | Neighbor type code: R router, S switch, I IGMP, H host, P phone, r repeater and others (the legend is printed above the table). |
| Platform | Hardware model, for example WS-C3560. |
| Port ID | The neighbor's port, the other end of the cable. |
MEMORY TIP
Local = my port. Port ID = their port. Read each line as "my Fas 0/1 connects to SW-1's Fas 0/15".
show cdp neighbors detail
Shortened from the book's output BOOK
SW-3# show cdp neighbors detail
Device ID: SW-1
Entry address(es):
Platform: cisco WS-C3560-24TS, Capabilities: Switch IGMP
Interface: FastEthernet0/1, Port ID (outgoing port): FastEthernet0/15
Holdtime : 135 sec
Version :
Cisco IOS Software, C3560 Software ... Version 12.2(55)SE5, RELEASE SOFTWARE
advertisement version: 2
VTP Management Domain: 'NULL'
Native VLAN: 1
Duplex: full
Management address(es):
- show cdp neighbors detail: everything in the summary plus IP address, IOS version, native VLAN, duplex and VTP domain.
- show cdp entry *: gives the same result as the detail command BOOK . (show cdp entry <name> shows one neighbor.)
- Use detail when you need the neighbor's IP address. The summary command never shows it.
EXAM CRITICAL
Which command gives the neighbor's IP address? show cdp neighbors detail. The book's own review question 4 tests exactly this. BOOK
WHAT THE BOOK SAYS
The book's "CDP Can Save Lives" story says an admin can rebuild a network map from CDP alone. True, but you still need login access to each device. CDP only helps if you can log in. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
The book text says SW-1 and SW-2 are "3650 switches", but the output shows WS-C3560. It is a typo for 3560. The book's detail output also repeats the line Device ID: SW-1 twice. UPDATED
Quick check 12.1.2
Q1. In show cdp neighbors, which column is the neighbor's own interface?
A. Local Intrfce
B. Port ID
C. Platform
D. Holdtme
Answer: B - Port ID is the remote port.
Q2. Why does your router not see the PCs and other routers behind a connected switch?
Answer: CDP only reaches directly connected neighbors - a switch does not forward CDP frames.
Q3. Which two commands show the same detailed neighbor information?
Answer: show cdp neighbors detail and show cdp entry * - the book states they are equivalent.
Q4. On SW-3 you see SW-2 Fas 0/5 ... Fas 0/5. What does that tell you?
Answer: SW-3's Fas 0/5 is cabled to SW-2's Fas 0/5 - Local Intrfce is mine, Port ID is theirs.
12.1.3 Documenting a Network Topology Using CDP

The book gives an exercise: you can only console into Lab_A. Use show running-config for the local IP addresses and show cdp neighbors for the neighbors, then draw the network. The rule: each remote router gets the next IP address in the link's range. BOOK
| Lab_A port | Lab_A IP | Neighbor (CDP) | Platform | Neighbor port | Neighbor IP (next address) |
Calculated by script: each local address is a /24 (mask 255.255.255.0, 254 hosts), and each "next address" ending in .2 lies inside the same subnet. Matches the book's Figure 12.3. ADDED
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The routers in this exercise (2501, 2514, 2620, 2621) are very old hardware. The method is what matters: local config + CDP neighbor output = topology. Also, the exam in v2.0 asks you to validate documentation, so practise the reverse: given a diagram and CDP output, spot what does not match. UPDATED
ADDED (NOT IN THE BOOK)

Documentation check (v2.0 skill). For every link in a diagram, compare: (1) hostname, (2) local port, (3) remote port, (4) platform. A mismatch means the diagram is wrong or the cable is in the wrong port. Use show cdp neighbors detail for IPs and software versions. ADDED
Quick check 12.1.3
Q1. Which two sources do you combine to document a router's links in this exercise?
Answer: show running-config and show cdp neighbors - the first gives your IPs, the second gives the neighbors.
Q2. Lab_A Fa0/1 is 192.168.18.1/24. What is the neighbor's address under the book's rule?
Answer: 192.168.18.2 - next IP in the /24.
Q3. A diagram says SW-1 Gi0/1 connects to SW-2 Gi0/1, but CDP on SW-1 shows Port ID Gi0/2. What is the likely conclusion?
Answer: The diagram or the cabling is wrong - CDP reports the real port.
12.1.4 Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP)
VERIFY
Tracker note. The book teaches LLDP on pages 346 to 347 but does not list it as its own heading in the table of contents. I numbered it 12.1.4 so it gets its own tracker row. UPDATED
LLDP is the IEEE 802.1AB standard. It gives about the same information as CDP but works with any vendor. BOOK
- LLDP-MED (Media Endpoint Discovery) is an enhanced version for voice. The book says LLDP and LLDP-MED are not compatible. BOOK
- LLDP must be enabled on the device before you can enable or disable it on an interface. BOOK
- LLDP works only on physical interfaces, and the book says it can discover up to one device per port. BOOK
- lldp run / no lldp run: turn LLDP on or off globally (affects all interfaces). BOOK
- lldp transmit / lldp receive (interface mode): control sending and receiving per port. Use the no form to stop. BOOK
Commands: the first lines are in the book; the show lines are added ADDED CHECK
SW-3(config)# lldp run
SW-3(config)# interface gi0/1
SW-3(config-if)# no lldp transmit
SW-3(config-if)# lldp receive
SW-3(config-if)# end
SW-3# show lldp neighbors
SW-3# show lldp neighbors detail
- lldp run: starts LLDP on every interface. Needed first, because LLDP is off by default.
- no lldp transmit: this port stops sending LLDP frames.
- lldp receive: this port still listens for neighbors.
- show lldp neighbors: summary list. detail adds IP, system description and capabilities.
Illustrative output CHECK
SW-3# show lldp
Global LLDP Information:
Status: ACTIVE
LLDP advertisements are sent every 30 seconds
LLDP hold time advertised is 120 seconds
LLDP interface reinitialisation delay is 2 seconds
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book never says LLDP is off by default on Cisco devices, but that is why show lldp neighbors is empty on a fresh switch. Cisco documentation lists default timer 30 s (range 5 to 65534), holdtime 120 s (0 to 65535) and reinit delay 2 s (2 to 5). You can change them with lldp timer, lldp holdtime and lldp reinit. UPDATED
COMMON MISTAKE
Expecting CDP and LLDP to talk to each other. A Cisco device can run both at the same time; a non-Cisco neighbor will only answer LLDP.
Quick check 12.1.4
Q1. Which discovery protocol works between Cisco and non-Cisco devices?
A. CDP
B. LLDP
C. VTP
D. DTP
Answer: B - LLDP is the IEEE standard 802.1AB.
Q2. You typed show lldp neighbors on a new switch and it is empty although the link is up. First thing to check?
Answer: Whether lldp run was configured - LLDP is off by default.
Q3. Which two commands set a port to listen for LLDP but not send it?
Answer: no lldp transmit and lldp receive - interface-mode commands.
Q4. Are LLDP and LLDP-MED compatible, according to the book?
Answer: No - the book says they are not compatible.
Book pages 347 to 348. NTP synchronises device clocks from a time server. Correct time is needed for: putting events in the right order, reading syslog data correctly and digital certificates. BOOK
Why timestamps alone are not enough
The book shows service timestamps log datetime msec so log messages carry a date and time. But a router's own clock may be wrong, so the stamp may be wrong. NTP makes the clock correct. BOOK
Book configuration BOOK
SF(config)# service timestamps log datetime msec
SF(config)# ntp server 172.16.10.1 version 4
- service timestamps log datetime msec: add the date, time and milliseconds to log messages.
- ntp server 172.16.10.1: this device becomes an NTP client of the server at 172.16.10.1.
- version 4: use NTP version 4. (Optional. NTPv4 is defined in RFC 5905.) CHECK
- ntp master: make this router or switch an NTP server that serves its own clock.
Verify NTP
Book output, re-aligned: a client that has not synchronised BOOK
SF# show ntp status
Clock is unsynchronized, stratum 16, no reference clock
SF# show ntp associations
address ref clock st when poll reach delay offset disp
* master (synced), # master (unsynced), + selected, - candidate, ~ configured
| Output | Meaning |
| Clock is unsynchronized | The device has not locked on to a time source. |
| stratum 16 | Unsynchronised. Valid synchronised values are 1 to 15; a lower number is closer to the reference clock. |
| ~172.16.10.1 | The tilde means this server is configured, not yet synchronised. |
| * before an address | This is the selected master and the clock is synced to it. |
| reach 0 | No replies received from that server. |
EXAM CRITICAL
Client = ntp server <ip>. Server = ntp master. Verify with show ntp status and show ntp associations. Stratum 16 = not synchronised. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
Three clarifications that the book skips or states loosely. UPDATED
1. NTP uses UDP port 123. If an ACL or firewall blocks UDP 123, the client stays at stratum 16 with reach 0.
2. ntp master with no number defaults to stratum 8 on Cisco IOS. Give it an explicit stratum, for example ntp master 3.
3. The book says stratum is a number from 1 to 15. In the NTP standard a reference clock is stratum 0 and a server directly attached to it is stratum 1; an unsynchronised Cisco device shows 16.
ADDED (NOT IN THE BOOK)

Security. By default a client trusts any server that answers. A rogue server can feed wrong time and break certificates and logs. The book only mentions NTP authentication in one sentence; it is beyond the scope of this chapter. ADDED
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

v2.0 note. NTP configuration is no longer a named objective in the v2.0 outline. Learn the client/server commands and how to read show ntp status anyway: it is cheap to learn, part of v1.1 and useful in every lab. UPDATED
Quick check 12.2
Q1. Which command makes a router an NTP client of 10.1.1.5?
A. ntp master 10.1.1.5
B. ntp server 10.1.1.5
C. clock sync 10.1.1.5
D. ntp client 10.1.1.5
Answer: B - ntp server points the device at a time source.
Q2. show ntp status says stratum 16. What does it mean?
Answer: The clock is not synchronised - 16 means no valid time source.
Q3. Which UDP port does NTP use?
Answer: 123 - blocked UDP 123 is a common reason NTP fails.
Q4. Which command turns a router into an NTP server using its own clock?
Answer: ntp master - optionally with a stratum number.

Book pages 348 to 352. Simple Network Management Protocol is an Application-layer protocol that lets agents on devices talk to a network management station (NMS). Examples of an NMS in the book: Cisco Prime and SolarWinds. BOOK
- The NMS polls the agent (a GET message) to collect statistics such as interface status or CPU. BOOK
- The agent sends a trap to the NMS when something happens, such as an interface going down. BOOK
- The NMS can also SET a value on the device. BOOK
- Data is stored in a MIB (Management Information Base). BOOK
| Version | Security | Book says | Notes |
| SNMPv1 | Community string in plain text | Rarely implemented today | Oldest. |
| SNMPv2c | Community string in plain text, no encryption | Adds GET BULK and INFORM; not really more secure than v1 | The "c" stands for community. |
| SNMPv3 | Authentication (MD5 or SHA) and encryption | Says it uses TCP and DES or "DES-256" | See corrections below. |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
Corrections to the SNMP text. UPDATED

1. The book (page 349, Exam Essentials and review answer 3) says SNMPv3 uses TCP. SNMP uses UDP by default: UDP 161 for requests to the agent and UDP 162 for traps and informs sent to the NMS. Some implementations can run over TCP, but that is not what defines v3.
2. "DES-256" is not a standard name. SNMPv3 privacy uses DES, 3DES or AES (AES-128, 192 or 256, depending on the platform).
3. SNMPv3 has three security levels: noAuthNoPriv (nothing), authNoPriv (authentication only), authPriv (authentication and encryption). v3 also uses user names, not community strings.
4. SHA and AES are the modern choices; MD5 and DES are legacy. CHECK
EXAM CRITICAL
Remember: v2c introduced GET BULK and INFORM (the book's review answer 3 agrees). v3 = security (authentication and encryption). v1 and v2c are plain-text community strings. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book says SNMP was created in 1988 (RFC 1065). RFC 1065 describes the structure of management information. The SNMPv1 protocol itself is RFC 1157 (1990). The exact RFC does not matter for the exam. UPDATED CHECK
12.3.1 Management Information Base (MIB)

A MIB is a hierarchical collection of manageable values. Each value has an OID (object identifier) that looks like a path through a tree, written in words or numbers. Top levels belong to standards bodies; vendors have private branches. BOOK
Cisco's branch, from the book's Figure 12.6 BOOK
iso (1) > org (3) > dod (6) > internet (1) > private (4) > enterprise (1) > cisco (9)
You do not need to memorise OIDs for the exam. BOOK
| Operation | Direction | What it does |
| GET | Manager asks agent | Read a value from the MIB. |
| SET | Manager tells agent | Write a value on the device. |
| WALK | Manager asks agent | Read a range of successive MIB objects. |
| TRAP | Agent to manager | Unsolicited alert. No acknowledgement. |
| INFORM | Agent to manager | Like a trap but acknowledged by the manager. |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
The book defines SET as "get information to the MIB from an SNMP agent". That is backwards. With SET the manager changes a value on the agent. UPDATED
Quick check 12.3.1
Q1. Which SNMP message is acknowledged by the manager?
A. TRAP
B. GET
C. INFORM
D. WALK
Answer: C - INFORM adds acknowledgement; a trap does not.
Q2. Which SNMP version first added GET BULK?
Answer: SNMPv2c - per the book and review answer 3.
Q3. What does the number string 1.3.6.1.4.1.9 point to?
Answer: Cisco's private enterprise branch of the MIB - the OID tree.
12.3.2 Configuring SNMP
Four steps in the book: read-write access, contact, location, and an ACL to limit who can use the community string. Only the community string is required. BOOK
Book configuration (the exit line is added so the last command runs in global mode) BOOK CHECK
Router(config)# snmp-server community Todd rw
Router(config)# snmp-server location Boulder
Router(config)# snmp-server contact Todd Lammle
Router(config)# ip access-list standard Protect_NMS_Station
Router(config-std-nacl)# permit host 192.168.10.254
Router(config-std-nacl)# exit
Router(config)# snmp-server community Todd Protect_NMS_Station rw
- snmp-server community Todd rw: creates community string Todd with read-write access. Use ro for read-only.
- snmp-server location Boulder and snmp-server contact Todd Lammle: text fields that help whoever troubleshoots later.
- ip access-list standard Protect_NMS_Station + permit host 192.168.10.254: only the NMS at 192.168.10.254 may use the community.
- ... community Todd Protect_NMS_Station rw: attach that ACL to the community string.
| Access | What the NMS may do |
| Read-only (ro) | Read MIB objects (not the community strings). No changes. |
| Read-write (rw) | Read and change MIB objects (not the community strings). |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book gets the ACL purpose wrong. It says the ACL "protects the NMS from access, not the actual devices with the agents". In fact the ACL attached to the community string decides which NMS hosts may query the agent on this router. It protects the router's SNMP agent. The book's review answer 1 (put the ACL on the RO community string) is correct and matches this. UPDATED
WARNING

Community strings are sent in clear text in v1 and v2c. rw with a guessable string lets anyone who reaches UDP 161 change the device. Prefer SNMPv3 with authPriv, and always use ro unless you really need writes. ADDED
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book says entering snmp-server enables SNMPv1 on the device. Current IOS versions support v1, v2c and v3, and the version used depends on how the manager is set up and what you configure. SNMPv3 needs snmp-server group and snmp-server user, which the book does not cover. UPDATED CHECK
Quick check 12.3.2
Q1. Which command is the only required SNMP command in the book's list?
Answer: snmp-server community <string> - location, contact and ACL are optional.
Q2. How do you restrict which NMS can use a read-only community?
A. ACL on the VTY line
B. ACL on the community string
C. ACL on every interface
D. ACL on the control plane
Answer: B - attach the ACL in the snmp-server community command.
Q3. You use an SNMP manager to change a router's hostname. Which community access is needed?
Answer: Read-write (rw) - ro cannot change anything.
Q4. Which direction does a TRAP travel?
Answer: Agent to NMS - unsolicited alert.
Book pages 352 to 356. Cisco devices produce messages for events such as an interface changing state. Syslog is the standard way to store them centrally. BOOK
Four places a device can send messages: logging buffer (RAM, on by default), console (on by default), terminal lines (needs terminal monitor), syslog server. BOOK
Message format
Format and the book's console example BOOK
seq no:timestamp: %facility-severity-MNEMONIC:description
*Oct 21 15:33:50.565: %LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface FastEthernet0/0, changed state to administratively down
| Part | Meaning |
| seq no | Sequence number. Not shown unless service sequence-numbers is on. |
| timestamp | Date and time. Shown only if timestamps are configured. |
| facility | The part of the system that produced it (here LINK). |
| severity | One digit, 0 to 7 (see table). |
| MNEMONIC | Short text that identifies the message. |
| description | Details of the event. |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
The book says severity is "a single-digit code from 0 to 5". It is 0 to 7. UPDATED
Severity levels (memorise)
| Level | Name | Meaning |
| 0 | Emergency | System is unusable. |
| 1 | Alert | Immediate action needed. |
| 2 | Critical | Critical condition. |
| 3 | Error | Error condition. |
| 4 | Warning | Warning condition. |
| 5 | Notification | Normal but significant condition. |
| 6 | Informational | Normal information message. |
| 7 | Debugging | Debugging messages. |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

Table 12.2 and the Exam Essentials table contain an error. The book lists "Debugging (severity 5)". Debugging is 7. The same mistake appears in the book's logging trap ? output (it shows <0-5> and "debugging (severity=5)"). The real range is <0-7> and debugging is 7. Do not memorise the book's table. This corrected table is the one to learn. Checked against Cisco community posts that show real IOS output (secondary). RFC 5424 uses the same 0 to 7 scale (general knowledge, not fetched). UPDATED
MEMORY TIP
Every Awesome Cisco Engineer Will Need Icecream Daily: Emergency 0, Alert 1, Critical 2, Error 3, Warning 4, Notification 5, Informational 6, Debugging 7. BOOK
EXAM CRITICAL
A severity level shows messages at that level and all lower numbers. logging trap 4 sends levels 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. A lower number is more severe. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book says "Level 5 is the highest-level security option and displays everything" and that it may hurt performance. In reality level 7 (debugging) shows everything, and debug output can strain a device. UPDATED
ADDED (NOT IN THE BOOK)

Facilities. Besides severity, a syslog message carries a facility value (for example local0 to local7). The Cisco default facility is local7. Severity says how serious; facility says which source or category. On the wire the two combine into one value: PRI = facility x 8 + severity. With local7 (23) and severity 6 (informational), PRI = 190. Calculated by script. The book's review question 7 expects local7. The v2.0 objective 5.6 names facilities explicitly. ADDED
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book also says (page 355) "The default trap level is debugging", but its own show logging output says Trap logging: level informational. The Cisco default for syslog-server logging (logging trap) is informational (6), which is also what the book's configuration example uses. The default for console and buffer logging is debugging (7). UPDATED CHECK
Quick check 12.4
Q1. What is severity 4?
A. Error
B. Warning
C. Notification
D. Critical
Answer: B - 0 Emerg, 1 Alert, 2 Crit, 3 Err, 4 Warning.
Q2. Which severity numbers are sent after logging trap 3?
Answer: 0, 1, 2, 3 - the level you set and all more severe levels.
Q3. What is the severity number of Debugging?
Answer: 7 - not 5, as the book's table wrongly shows.
Q4. In %LINK-5-CHANGED, what does the 5 mean?
Answer: Severity 5 (Notification) - second field after the facility.
12.4.1 Configuring and Verifying Syslog
Book commands BOOK
Router(config)# logging console
Router(config)# logging buffered
Router(config)# no logging console
Router(config)# no logging buffered
Router# show logging
- logging console / logging buffered: send messages to the console or to the RAM buffer (both are on by default).
- no logging console / no logging buffered: turn them off.
- show logging: shows what is enabled, each destination's level and the buffer contents.
Shortened from the book's output BOOK
Router# show logging
Syslog logging: enabled (11 messages dropped, 1 messages rate-limited, ...)
Console logging: level debugging, 29 messages logged ...
Monitor logging: level debugging, 0 messages logged ...
Buffer logging: level debugging, 1 messages logged ...
Trap logging: level informational, 33 message lines logged
Log Buffer (4096 bytes):
*Jun 21 23:09:35.822: %SYS-5-CONFIG_I: Configured from console by console
Send messages to a syslog server
Book configuration, with timestamps and sequence numbers BOOK
SF(config)# logging 172.16.10.1
SF(config)# logging trap informational
SF(config)# service timestamps log datetime msec
SF(config)# service sequence-numbers
- logging 172.16.10.1: send messages to the syslog server at that address. The book usually writes logging host 172.16.10.1; both work. BOOK
- logging trap informational: only levels 0 to 6 go to the server. You can use the name or the number (logging trap 6).
- service timestamps log datetime msec: add a date and time to each message.
- service sequence-numbers: add a sequence number (the book first runs no service timestamps, which then shows the number instead of the time).
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book calls the logging trap levels "local levels (for example local6)" and says there is no difference. That mixes two ideas. Local0 to local7 are facilities, not severity levels. The severity range 0 to 7 is separate. UPDATED
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

Syslog transport is normally UDP port 514 (RFC 5424 defines the message format). Many servers also accept TCP or TLS. Port numbers and RFC details are general knowledge here, not verified against a Cisco page in this session. ADDED CHECK
COMMON MISTAKE

Setting a very high level (7) on a busy device sends a flood of debug messages. Also check that the router can reach the syslog server; a wrong IP means messages vanish with no error. Use terminal monitor if you are in a Telnet or SSH session and see nothing.
Quick check 12.4.1
Q1. Which destinations are on by default?
Answer: Console and buffer - per the book.
Q2. Which command shows the buffer and the level of each logging destination?
Answer: show logging - also shows the trap level.
Q3. You are in an SSH session and no log messages appear on screen. Which command fixes that?
Answer: terminal monitor - VTY lines do not get log messages unless enabled.
Q4. What does logging trap informational do?
Answer: Sends severities 0 to 6 to the syslog server - levels at or more severe than informational.
Book pages 357 to 358. Telnet sends everything, including the username and password, in clear text. SSH encrypts the session. The book strongly recommends SSH. BOOK
The book's steps
Book commands BOOK
Router(config)# hostname Todd
Todd(config)# ip domain-name Lammle.com
Todd(config)# username Todd password Lammle
Todd(config)# crypto key generate rsa
How many bits in the modulus [512]: 1024
Todd(config)# ip ssh version 2
Todd(config)# line vty 0 15
Todd(config-line)# login local
Todd(config-line)# transport input ssh
- hostname Todd: set a hostname other than the default. Needed to name the keys.
- ip domain-name Lammle.com: set the domain. The key name becomes Todd.Lammle.com. Hostname and domain name are both required to generate the keys.
- username Todd password Lammle: a local user for SSH login.
- crypto key generate rsa: make the RSA key pair. Pick the modulus size when asked.
- ip ssh version 2: allow only SSH version 2. Optional but recommended.
- line vty 0 15: enter the 16 virtual terminal lines.
- login local: check logins against the local username database.
- transport input ssh: allow only SSH on those lines.
EXAM CRITICAL

To generate SSH keys you need: a hostname (not the default), a domain name, then crypto key generate rsa. For logins you also need a local user and login local. The book's review answer 11 lists username, domain name, login local, transport input ssh and the crypto key command. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

Key size. The book prompt suggests 512 bits and the book uses 1024. SSH version 2 needs a key of at least 768 bits (Cisco documentation). Use 2048 bits or more in real networks. The book's prompt shows a range of 360 to 4096; limits vary by IOS version. UPDATED CHECK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

Passwords. The book uses username Todd password Lammle, which is stored weakly. Use username Todd privilege 15 secret <password> so the password is hashed. Do not reuse a book password in a lab you keep. Also use a K9 (crypto) image: SSH is not available on images without crypto features. UPDATED ADDED
WARNING
The book warns against transport input all in production. transport input ssh telnet allows both. If you leave out telnet, only SSH works. BOOK
Verify SSH
Illustrative commands and output ADDED CHECK
Todd# show ip ssh
SSH Enabled - version 2.0
Todd# show ssh
Todd# show crypto key mypubkey rsa
- show ip ssh: is SSH enabled, and which version.
- show ssh: lists active SSH sessions.
- show crypto key mypubkey rsa: shows the RSA key pair that was generated.
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

v2.0 note. SFTP and SCP (copying files over SSH) are new in v2.0 objective 4.2 and are not taught in this book. Learn SSH properly first. Then see the Cisco documentation for ip scp server enable and copy scp:. ADDED CHECK
Quick check 12.5
Q1. Which two settings are required before crypto key generate rsa works?
Answer: A non-default hostname and an IP domain name - the key name is built from both.
Q2. Which VTY command allows only SSH?
A. transport input all
B. transport input telnet
C. transport input ssh
D. login local
Answer: C - login local only picks the authentication source.
Q3. Why is SSH better than Telnet?
Answer: It encrypts the session, including the password - Telnet sends data in clear text.
Q4. What does login local do?
Answer: Tells the line to authenticate against local usernames - created with username.

Nothing in this document was run on real Cisco hardware. All commands and outputs marked CHECK are illustrative. Record what you actually see in your labs.
Default tool: Cisco Packet Tracer. Record what you actually saw in the Self-Assessment table. Packet Tracer does not behave exactly like real IOS, so every expected result is marked CHECK .
VERIFY

Packet Tracer limits (not tested by me): some versions have no LLDP commands, NTP and SNMP support is partial, and SSH key sizes or show output may differ. If a command is missing, say so in your notes and try it on virtual IOS (for example CML or GNS3) or real equipment. CHECK
Topology: two switches (SW1, SW2) joined by one cable, and a router R1 attached to SW1.
- Give each device a hostname and a management address.
- On SW1 run show cdp. Write the timer and holdtime.
- Run show cdp neighbors and show cdp neighbors detail. Write which neighbors, ports and IPs you see.
- On SW1 interface to SW2 run no cdp enable. Wait, then run show cdp neighbors on both switches.
- Run cdp enable again. Try cdp timer 10 and cdp holdtime 30, then show cdp.
- Enable LLDP: lldp run on both switches. Run show lldp neighbors and show lldp neighbors detail.
- Draw the topology from the output only, then compare with the real cabling.
Step 4 CHECK
SW1(config)# interface gi0/1
SW1(config-if)# no cdp enable
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show cdp neighbors
- no cdp enable: stops CDP on that port only.
- show cdp neighbors: the neighbor should disappear on the other switch after its holdtime runs out.

Expected result: after step 3 you see SW2 and R1 with the correct local and remote ports. After step 4 SW2 drops out of SW1's table only when the holdtime expires (up to 180 s by default). In step 6 LLDP shows nothing until lldp run is entered. CHECK
- Router R1 will be the NTP server. Give it a clock: clock set in privileged mode, then ntp master 3.
- Router R2 is the client. Configure ntp server <R1 address>. Ping R1 first.
- On R2 run show ntp status and show ntp associations. Repeat every minute for a few minutes.
- On R2 enable service timestamps log datetime msec.
- Add a syslog server (a PC with the syslog service in Packet Tracer): logging <server IP> and logging trap informational.
- Shut and re-enable an interface on R2 and look at the server log and show logging.
- Change to logging trap errors, repeat, and notice which messages disappear.
Key commands CHECK
R1(config)# ntp master 3
R2(config)# ntp server 10.0.0.1
R2# show ntp status
R2(config)# logging 10.0.0.50
R2(config)# logging trap informational
- ntp master 3: R1 serves its own clock at stratum 3.
- ntp server 10.0.0.1: R2 asks R1 for time.
- logging 10.0.0.50: send syslog messages to the server.
- logging trap informational: levels 0 to 6 are sent.

Expected result: R2 starts at stratum 16, then moves to stratum 4 (one more than R1) after some minutes if all works. Link up/down messages (level 5 notification) appear at the server with informational, but not with errors because 5 is less severe than 3. CHECK
- On a router configure snmp-server community cisco-ro ro, a location and a contact.
- Run show snmp and show run | include snmp.
- Create the ACL permit host <NMS IP> and attach it to the community string.
- If your simulator has an SNMP manager, query the router with the correct and the wrong community string. Otherwise note that you only verified the configuration, not the polling.
Expected result: the configuration appears in show run; counters in show snmp change when a manager polls. CHECK
- Set hostname and domain name. Create a user with a secret.
- Run crypto key generate rsa with 1024 bits. Confirm show ip ssh.
- Set ip ssh version 2. Configure line vty 0 15 with login local and transport input ssh.
- From a PC, try Telnet (should fail), then SSH (should work).
- Remove the domain name and try to generate keys again to see the error.
Lab configuration CHECK
Router(config)# hostname R1
R1(config)# ip domain-name lab.local
R1(config)# username admin privilege 15 secret LabPass123
R1(config)# crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024
R1(config)# ip ssh version 2
R1(config)# line vty 0 15
R1(config-line)# login local
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
- crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024: skips the question and sets the size directly.
- username admin privilege 15 secret ...: a hashed password and full privilege.
- transport input ssh: Telnet connections are now refused.

content.text: Q1 What are the default CDP timer and holdtime?
Answer: 60 s and 180 s - the receiver keeps a neighbor for 180 s.
Q2 Which command stops CDP on one interface only?
A. no cdp run
B. no cdp enable
C. cdp holdtime 0
D. no cdp timer
Answer: B - no cdp enable is per interface; no cdp run is global.
Q3 A neighbor disappears from the CDP table after a while although the cable is fine. Which value expired?
Answer: The holdtime - no CDP packet arrived within the holdtime.
Q1 In show cdp neighbors, which column is the neighbor's own interface?
A. Local Intrfce
B. Port ID
C. Platform
D. Holdtme
Answer: B - Port ID is the remote port.
Q2 Why does your router not see the PCs and other routers behind a connected switch?
Answer: C - DP only reaches directly connected neighbors - a switch does not forward CDP frames.
Q3 Which two commands show the same detailed neighbor information?
Answer: show cdp neighbors detail and show cdp entry * - the book states they are equivalent.
Q4 On SW-3 you see SW-2 Fas 0/5 ... Fas 0/5. What does that tell you?
Answer: SW-3's Fas 0/5 is cabled to SW-2's Fas 0/5 - Local Intrfce is mine, Port ID is theirs.
Q1 Which two sources do you combine to document a router's links in this exercise?
Answer: show running-config and show cdp neighbors - the first gives your IPs, the second gives the neighbors.
Q2 Lab_A Fa0/1 is 192.168.18.1/24. What is the neighbor's address under the book's rule?
Answer: 192.168.18.2 - next IP in the /24.
Q3 A diagram says SW-1 Gi0/1 connects to SW-2 Gi0/1, but CDP on SW-1 shows Port ID Gi0/2. What is the likely conclusion?
Answer: The diagram or the cabling is wrong - CDP reports the real port.
Q1 Which discovery protocol works between Cisco and non-Cisco devices?
A. CDP
B. LLDP
C. VTP
D. DTP
Answer: B - LLDP is the IEEE standard 802.1AB.
Q2 You typed show lldp neighbors on a new switch and it is empty although the link is up. First thing to check?
Answer: Whether lldp run was configured - LLDP is off by default.
Q3 Which two commands set a port to listen for LLDP but not send it?
Answer: no lldp transmit and lldp receive - interface-mode commands.
Q4 Are LLDP and LLDP-MED compatible, according to the book?
Answer: No - the book says they are not compatible.
Q1 Which command makes a router an NTP client of 10.1.1.5?
A. ntp master 10.1.1.5
B. ntp server 10.1.1.5
C. clock sync 10.1.1.5
D. ntp client 10.1.1.5
Answer: B - ntp server points the device at a time source.
Q2 show ntp status says stratum 16. What does it mean?
Answer: The clock is not synchronised - 16 means no valid time source.
Q3 Which UDP port does NTP use?
Answer: 123 - blocked UDP 123 is a common reason NTP fails.
Q4 Which command turns a router into an NTP server using its own clock?
Answer: ntp master - optionally with a stratum number.
Q1 Which SNMP message is acknowledged by the manager?
A. TRAP
B. GET
C. INFORM
D. WALK
Answer: C - INFORM adds acknowledgement; a trap does not.
Q2 Which SNMP version first added GET BULK?
Answer: SNMPv2c - per the book and review answer 3.
Q3 What does the number string 1.3.6.1.4.1.9 point to?
Answer: C - isco's private enterprise branch of the MIB - the OID tree.
Q1 Which command is the only required SNMP command in the book's list?
Answer: snmp-server community <string> - location, contact and ACL are optional.
Q2 How do you restrict which NMS can use a read-only community?
A. ACL on the VTY line
B. ACL on the community string
C. ACL on every interface
D. ACL on the control plane
Answer: B - attach the ACL in the snmp-server community command.
Q3 You use an SNMP manager to change a router's hostname. Which community access is needed?
Answer: Read-write (rw) - ro cannot change anything.
Q4 Which direction does a TRAP travel?
Answer: A - gent to NMS - unsolicited alert.
Q1 What is severity 4?
A. Error
B. Warning
C. Notification
D. Critical
Answer: B - 0 Emerg, 1 Alert, 2 Crit, 3 Err, 4 Warning.
Q2 Which severity numbers are sent after logging trap 3?
Answer: 0, 1, 2, 3 - the level you set and all more severe levels.
Q3 What is the severity number of Debugging?
Answer: 7 - not 5, as the book's table wrongly shows.
Q4 In %LINK-5-CHANGED, what does the 5 mean?
Answer: Severity 5 (Notification) - second field after the facility.
Q1 Which destinations are on by default?
Answer: C - onsole and buffer - per the book.
Q2 Which command shows the buffer and the level of each logging destination?
Answer: show logging - also shows the trap level.
Q3 You are in an SSH session and no log messages appear on screen. Which command fixes that?
Answer: terminal monitor - VTY lines do not get log messages unless enabled.
Q4 What does logging trap informational do?
Answer: Sends severities 0 to 6 to the syslog server - levels at or more severe than informational.
Q1 Which two settings are required before crypto key generate rsa works?
Answer: A - non-default hostname and an IP domain name - the key name is built from both.
Q2 Which VTY command allows only SSH?
A. transport input all
B. transport input telnet
C. transport input ssh
D. login local
Answer: C - login local only picks the authentication source.
Q3 Why is SSH better than Telnet?
Answer: It encrypts the session, including the password - Telnet sends data in clear text.
Q4 What does login local do?
Answer: Tells the line to authenticate against local usernames - created with username.
Q1 Which protocol is Cisco proprietary?
A. LLDP
B. CDP
C. NTP
D. SNMP
Answer: B - CDP only runs between Cisco devices.
Q2 Which command lists the neighbor's IP address?
A. show cdp
B. show cdp neighbors
C. show cdp neighbors detail
D. show lldp
Answer: C - detail includes the IP address.
Q3 Default CDP timer and holdtime?
Answer: B - 60 s and 180 s.
Q4 Which command enables LLDP globally?
A. lldp enable
B. lldp run
C. cdp run lldp
D. lldp start
Answer: B - lldp run.
Q5 A switch connects to a router. You run show cdp neighbors on the router. What do you see?
Answer: Only the switch (directly connected) - devices behind the switch are not shown.
Q6 In show cdp neighbors, the Port ID column shows which port?
Answer: The neighbor's port - Local Intrfce is yours.
Q7 Which NTP command makes a router an NTP client?
Answer: ntp server <ip> - client points to a server.
Q8 show ntp status says stratum 16. Name two possible causes.
Answer: Server unreachable; UDP 123 blocked; wrong server IP; server unsynchronised - any two.
Q9 Which UDP port does NTP use?
Answer: A - SNMP uses 161/162, syslog 514.
Q10 Which SNMP message is sent by the agent without being asked and is not acknowledged?
A. GET
B. SET
C. TRAP
D. INFORM
Answer: C - INFORM is acknowledged.
Q11 Which SNMP version first offers authentication and encryption?
A. v1
B. v2c
C. v3
D. v2
Answer: C - authPriv in v3.
Q12 Which transport does SNMP use by default?
Answer: UDP (161 and 162) - the book wrongly says SNMPv3 uses TCP.
Q13 True or false: the ACL on the community string protects the router's SNMP agent.
Answer: True - it restricts which NMS hosts may query the agent.
Q14 Which community type gives read-only access?
Answer: ro - rw allows changes.
Q15 What severity is Notification?
Answer: B - 0 Emerg, 1 Alert, 2 Crit, 3 Err, 4 Warn, 5 Notif, 6 Info, 7 Debug.
Q16 After logging trap warnings, which severities reach the server?
Answer: 0 to 4 - levels at or more severe than 4.
Q17 Which command shows what the buffer holds and each logging level?
Answer: show logging - it lists each destination and its level.
Q18 What is the default syslog facility on Cisco IOS?
A. local0
B. local4
C. local7
D. kern
Answer: C - local7.
Q19 In the message %SYS-5-CONFIG_I, what is SYS?
Answer: The facility - 5 is the severity and CONFIG_I is the mnemonic.
Q20 You are logged in over SSH and want to see log messages on your screen. Command?
Answer: terminal monitor - VTY sessions need it.
Q21 What stops you from using crypto key generate rsa on a default-hostname router?
Answer: Missing hostname or domain name - both are needed for the key name.
Q22 Which command line allows only SSH on the VTY lines?
Answer: transport input ssh - applied under the VTY lines.
Q23 Minimum RSA key size for SSH version 2?
Answer: B - 768 bits, but use 2048 or more.
Q24 Why use secret instead of password for a local user?
Answer: secret stores a hashed password - password is weaker.
Q25 Which v2.0 objective covers syslog severity levels and facilities?
Answer: 5.6 - SNMP is 5.4; CDP/LLDP is 2.3.
